charts.title: Prevalence of obesity among adults aged 18 and over in the U.S. from 2011 to 2022
charts.short: Obesity prevalence among U.S. adults aged 18 and over 2011-2022
charts.description: The prevalence of obesity in the United States has risen gradually over the past decade. As of 2022, around 33 percent of the population aged 18 years and older was obese. Obesity is a growing problem in many parts of the world but is particularly troubling in the United States.
charts.note: United States; 18 years and older
charts.source: CDC (BRFSS)

charts.title: Percentage of adults with obesity in the United States as of 2022, by state
charts.short: Percentage of obese U.S. adults by state 2022
charts.description: West Virginia, Louisiana, and Oklahoma are the U.S. states with the highest percentage of their population who are obese. The states with the lowest percentage of their population who are obese include Colorado, Hawaii, and Vermont.
charts.note: United States
charts.source: CDC Percentage of adults

charts.title: Percentage of adults that were physically inactive in the United States from 2017-2020, by state
charts.short: Percentage of physically inactive U.S. adults by state 2017-2020
charts.description: This statistic represents the percentage of adults in the United States that have done no physical activity or exercise within the preceding 30 days, from 2017 to 2020. During this time, Mississippi had the highest rate of physical inactivity among U.S. states with 33.2 percent of adults reporting no physical activity or exercise besides their job. The state of Colorado had the lowest rates of physical inactivity at this time.
charts.note: United States; 2017-2020; 18 years and older
charts.source: CDC (BRFSS) Percentage of adults

charts.title: Prevalence of severe obesity among U.S. adults from 2017 to March 2020, by age group
charts.short: Severe obesity prevalence among U.S. adults 2017-2020, by age group
charts.description: From 2017 to March 2020, the prevalence of severe obesity in the United States was highest among those aged 40-59 years. This statistic shows the age-adjusted prevalence of severe obesity among U.S. adults aged 20 and over from 2017 to March 2020, by age group.
charts.note: United States; 20 years and older
charts.source: CDC (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES))

charts.title: Prevalence of severe obesity among U.S. adults aged 20 and older from 2017 to March 2020, by gender
charts.short: Prevalence of severe obesity among adults in the U.S. 2017-2020, by gender
charts.description: From 2017 to March 2020, the prevalence of severe obesity in U.S. adults was 9.2 percent and was higher in women than men. This statistic shows the age-adjusted prevalence of severe obesity among adults aged 20 and over in the United States from 2017 to March 2020, by gender.
charts.note: United States; 2017 to March 2020; 20 years and older
charts.source: CDC (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES))

charts.title: Prevalence of severe obesity among U.S. adults from 2017 to March 2020, by race/ethnicity
charts.short: Severe obesity prevalence among U.S. adults 2017-2020, by race/ethnicity
charts.description: From 2017 to March 2020, the prevalence of severe obesity in the U.S. was highest among non-Hispanic blacks. This statistic shows the age-adjusted prevalence of severe obesity among U.S. adults aged 20 and over from 2017 to March 2020, by race/ethnicity.
charts.note: United States; 20 years and older
charts.source: CDC (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES))
